content:
"Make this: Instead of setting fire to, chopping up, or throwing away the woody stems and branches left after winter pruning, turn them into a useful dead hedge. It is a simple, wildlife-friendly structure that can shelter the garden from wind, create habitat for insects, birds and small mammals, and help separate one part of your growing space from another. Drive sturdy stakes, old posts or similar supports into the ground in two parallel lines, leaving about 50cm between them. Then pack the gap with your cuttings, placing the thicker branches low down to give the hedge a firm base. Keep adding twiggy material as you have it, remembering that the contents will gradually sink and compact.

Read this: If your Christmas presents were disappointing, lift your spirits by ordering The Book of Seeds by Paul Smith, formerly of Kew’s Millennium Seed Bank. Published by Ivy Press, this £30 volume celebrates 600 remarkable seeds, including tiny orchid seeds and strange, hairy examples.

Plant this: For winter colour, try Clematis cirrhosa in a warm, protected, sunny position. ‘Advent Bells’, var. balearica and ‘Jingle Bells’ offer beautiful blooms during the coldest months. Is there anything else I can help with?"
